# crawl.cheap — Complete Knowledge Corpus

> Open-source, Cloudflare-native web data engine that speaks the Firecrawl v2 API. Scrape, crawl, map, search, extract, parse, run AI Search (RAG) and persistent interactive browser sessions — at roughly half Firecrawl’s price. Point an existing Firecrawl client at crawl.cheap and keep your code.

MIT-licensed; self-hostable on your own Cloudflare account with no dependency on crawl.cheap.
Firecrawl v2 compatibility = change the base URL + swap in a crawl.cheap `cc_` key; request/response business logic is unchanged.
One Cloudflare Worker terminates the REST API; a second serves the marketing site + remote MCP.

## API

### Firecrawl v2-compatible REST API
Source: https://api.crawl.cheap

## Firecrawl v2-compatible REST API

Base URL `https://api.crawl.cheap`. Every endpoint mirrors the Firecrawl v2 request/response contract, so an existing Firecrawl client works after changing only the base URL and the API key (use a crawl.cheap `cc_` key, never a Firecrawl `fc-` key).

- `POST /v2/scrape` — fetch one URL as clean markdown / HTML / links / screenshot.
- `POST /v2/map` — enumerate a site’s URLs from sitemaps + link discovery.
- `POST /v2/crawl` — recursively crawl a site with include/exclude rules.
- `POST /v2/batch/scrape` — scrape many URLs in one job.
- `POST /v2/search` — web / news / images search with `tbs` time filters.
- `POST /v2/extract` — structured JSON extraction against a schema.
- `POST /v2/parse` — parse an already-fetched document.
- `POST /v2/agent` — autonomous multi-step research.
- `POST /v2/monitor` — scheduled change detection.
- `POST /v2/browser` — persistent interactive browser sessions.
- `POST /v2/ai-search` — semantic RAG over crawled content.

### Remote MCP server
Source: https://crawl-cheap-mcp.manhattan.workers.dev/v2/mcp

## Remote MCP server

A stateless Streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC MCP endpoint at `https://crawl-cheap-mcp.manhattan.workers.dev/v2/mcp`. It exposes `firecrawl_*` tools (scrape, map, crawl, search, agent, monitor, research) so an MCP-capable agent can use crawl.cheap directly as a first-class tool provider.
